questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study geology and I wanted to go to a place where the geology was significantly different from the Danish. Another important aspect for me was the surrounding nature since I love hiking and wanted to go a place with beautiful nature and lots of hiking opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved Tasmania and Hobart, but I was surprised how much time I had to spent on studying compared to home and I found it more difficult getting into a new university's style of teaching as I had expected.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the host university was very helpful and easy to contact.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university is very welcoming and helpful with everything. They have an introduction for all new students upon arrival where all the necessary practical stuff is presented and explained.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There is a contact person for all exchange students who is always accessible in her office.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a rental house together with three others Danes. It took some time before we found it and in the meantime we were living at a hostel, but I think it was worth it. The student accommodation is expensive and a lot of the other exchange students found rental rooms in sharehouses, which also sounded as a great experience.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for cold temperatures! The housed here are not insulated and the prizes for power are high (!) so bring an extra sweater, woolen socks and bring the blanket from the flight ;)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The website is very easily understandable and the host university is good and quick at answering any questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I e-mailed with the host university before arrival and talked to the exchange coordinator upon arrival, both worked perfectly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry, you can always change your choices once you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the teaching was online, which I didn't like.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was quite high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: they have a mix of different types of classes, with some of them being online and some physical. I like the UCPH way better, but that might be because that's what I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geological mapping
Mineral exploration geology
Introduction to Antarctic science B
Deep Earth

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed Mineral Exploration and Introduction to Antarctic science B. 
But all of the courses were great and had field trips, which was a great way to meet the classmates.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: they have a variety of different clubs and societies that you can join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the TUSA salsa society which has classes in salsa, bachata, swing and zouk for good prizes each Tuesday. This was amazing and a great way to meet locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go hiking as much as possible! Tasmanias nature is so beautiful and you really need to just go out there and explore. There are a range of several-day hikes which i highly recommend doing one or more of. 
Some of the ones I did and would recommend are:
- The Overland track (expensive but worth it!)
- the three capes
- Mount Anne circuit (very difficult but so beautiful - but spend 3 days even though its not that long a walk, the terrain is tough. )
All of the several day hikes needs booking, so plan ahead.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the locals are very friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join some of the soceities and clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is build for cars, so if you dont have access to a car it is quite difficult to get around. I bought a mountainbike to go around town, which I can recommend - there are a lot of hills.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals are more open and easier to talk to than Danes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Don't worry too much about courses and registration prior to arrival, it is easy to make changes once you arrive. 
- Prioritize to bring necessary gear for hiking (boots, rain clothes, sleeping bag, sleeping mat) you are gonna use it a lot if you like nature.
- Bring warm clothes! it is cold and can be snowing in the mountains even in the summer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It will be a great experience - remember to plan some time for travelling and seeing Tasmania after the semester ends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of great people and experiencing some amazing nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to studying at a different university with a different style and system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
